Hazards_Annotation: Heavy rainfall, flash floods, widespread power outages, and crop damages are reported.

Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Southeast Texas, notably Orange County, suffered major power outages and wind impacts.
Main_Event_Annotation: Event recorded as Hurricane Laura.
Hazards_Annotation: High wind gusts, power outages, and carbon monoxide poisoning incidents are emphasized.

Time_Annotation: Mid-September 2020 – Tropical Storm Beta brings extensive rainfall across southeast Texas.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Areas in and around Houston, including Brooks, Texas are affected.

Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Impacted the Texas Gulf Coast and Tamaulipas with a fatal rip current in Galveston.

Main_Event_Annotation: Event designated as Hurricane Beryl.

Main_Event_Annotation: Identified as Tropical Depression Nine, a type of tropical cyclone.
Hazards_Annotation: The report mentions 30 mph winds, a storm surge peaking at 3 ft, and damage from strong thunderstorm winds indicative of wind and flood hazards.

Time_Annotation: Early–June 2001 – Tropical Storm Allison makes landfall near Freeport, Texas on June 5 and then a second landfall on Morgan City on June 11.
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: The storm hit near Freeport, Texas and Morgan City in Louisiana, causing catastrophic flooding across Louisiana.
Main_Event_Annotation: Identified as Tropical Storm Allison, a tropical cyclone event.
Hazards_Annotation: It produced high winds, catastrophic flooding, and even tornado damage in Zachary.

Main_Event_Annotation: Identified as Tropical Storm Bertha, a tropical cyclone event.

Main_Event_Annotation: Identified as Tropical Storm Hanna, a tropical cyclone.

Time_Annotation: July 5, 2005 – Hurricane Cindy brought wind gusts of 70 mph to New Orleans.

Time_Annotation: August 2, 1995- Hurricane Erin strikes near Vero Beach and days later near Fort Walton Beach, producing moderate rainfall including totals of 10.14 inches (258 mm) in Melbourne and 20 inches (510 mm) in DeFuniak Springs on the Florida Panhandle. Thousands of homes are damaged near the hurricane's two landfalls, with monetary damage totaling about $700 million (1995 USD, $990 million 2008 USD). Rip currents kill a surfer off Palm Beach County, and two people die in the Gulf of Mexico when their boat capsizes.[76]
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Strikes near Vero Beach and Fort Walton Beach with impacts in Melbourne, DeFuniak Springs, and Palm Beach County
Main_Event_Annotation: Hurricane Erin making landfall and affecting multiple regions in Florida
Hazards_Annotation: Moderate rainfall, rip currents, and significant damage indicate both wind and flood hazards

Time_Annotation: August 23, 1995- Tropical Storm Jerry makes landfall near Jupiter and drops heavy rainfall throughout the state which peaks at 16.8 inches (430 mm) near Naples. Freshwater flooding from the rainfall damages 340 homes in Collier County, with damage amounting to $20.5 million (1995 USD, $29 million 2008 USD).[77]
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Makes landfall near Jupiter, affecting Collier County and Naples in Florida
Main_Event_Annotation: Tropical Storm Jerry making landfall
Hazards_Annotation: Heavy rainfall and resultant freshwater flooding are the major hazards

Time_Annotation: October 4, 1995- Hurricane Opal hits Pensacola Beach with winds of 115 mph (185 km/h). The hurricane drops moderate rainfall across much of the state, and a tornado spawned by Opal kills one person — the only direct casualty in the state from the hurricane. Strong winds and rough seas damage or destroy large portions of coastal towns along the Florida Panhandle, with serious damage extending eastward to Apalachicola. At the time, Opal is the third costliest tropical cyclone in the United States, with damage totaling over $1 billion (1995 USD) in Florida.[66]
Administrative_Areas_Annotation: Affects Pensacola Beach, the Florida Panhandle, and areas extending to Apalachicola
Main_Event_Annotation: Hurricane Opal making landfall and causing widespread damage
Hazards_Annotation: High winds, tornadoes, and heavy rainfall causing rough seas and damage are indicated

Time_Annotation: July 11, 1996- Hurricane Bertha parallels the east coast of Florida about 175 miles (282 km) offshore, producing a storm tide of 2 feet (0.61 m) at Jacksonville Beach, as well as rip currents along the coast. Time_Annotation: September 25, 1998 – Hurricane Georges passes over Key West as a Category 2 hurricane, and days later it moves eastward through the Florida Panhandle after hitting Biloxi, Mississippi. In the Florida Keys, the hurricane produced 8.41 inches (214 mm) of rain in Tavernier and wind gusts peaking at 110 mph (175 km/h) in Marathon. There, Georges damages 1,363 homes and destroys 173 houses, with damage amounting to $270 million (1998 USD) in the Keys. In the Florida Panhandle, the storm drops 38.46 inches (977 mm) of rain in Munson and results in $70 million in damage (1998 USD, $93 million 2008 USD).[86][87]
